entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Field Marshal Sir George Nugent, 1st Baronet, was a British Army officer. After serving as a junior officer in the American Revolutionary War, he fought with the Coldstream Guards under the Duke of York during the Flanders Campaign. He then commanded the Buckinghamshire Volunteers in the actions of St. Andria and Thuyl on the river Waal and participated in the disastrous retreat from the Rhine. He went on to be commander of the northern district of Ireland, in which post he played an important part in placating the people of Belfast during the Irish Rebellion, and then became Adjutant-General in Ireland.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As commander of the northern district of Ireland, Nugent played a crucial role in placating the people of Belfast during the Irish Rebellion, helping to mitigate the conflict's impact. His actions demonstrate his importance as a regional figure in 18th-century Irish history.
